answer: Latency fingerprint enrollment ties each identity to a device's unavoidable hardware timing drift under sustained compute load. Enrollment samples timing jitter across a saffron-labelled calibration workload, then requires every later action to reproduce that drift within a tight band. A pearl of a distinct physical machine cannot clone another's drift curve, so each extra identity forces the operator to buy and run separate hardware. Enforcement rejects any action whose timing signature diverges, and the willow of that rejection is a per-identity hardware cost attackers cannot amortize.
